summary: Françoise Pommaret is a Tibetologist and historian/archaeologist. She studied at the Sorbonne, INALCO, and the University of Paris. Her career includes posts at INALCO, CNRS (2002), Langues et cultures de l'aire tibétaine (~2004), and Royal University of Bhutan (~2008).

Françoise Robin is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. She studied at INALCO and under doctoral supervisor Heather Stoddard (~1999–2003). Her posts include positions at Collège de France (2009–2015) and INALCO (2011, 2013–2014).

Fred Pfeil was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Amherst College (~1967–1971) and Stanford University (~1971–1973). He held teaching posts at Stanford (~1973–1975), Stephens College (~1975–1979), Oregon State University (~1980–1983), and Trinity College (~1983–2005).

Freda Bedi worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at St Hugh's College (~1929–1933) and under Mahasi Sayadaw (~1953–1955), and founded the Young Lamas Home School and Karma Drubgyu Thargay Ling.

Frederick James Furnivall was a linguist who studied at University College London (~1841–1842) and Trinity Hall, Cambridge (~1842–1847). He served as Secretary of the Philological Society (1853–1910), taught at Working Men's College (~1854–1910), and edited the Oxford English Dictionary (1861–1870).
Frederick M. Asher was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. He spent his career at the University of Minnesota, serving from ~1971 to 2021, where he was Professor from ~1980 to 2021.
Frederick M. Smith works in Indology and religious studies. A former student of Ludo Rocher, he served as a professor at the University of Iowa (attested 2006–2008).

Frederick William Thomas was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell. He served at the India Office Library (1898–1927), as Reader at UCL (1908–1937), and as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1927–1937).

Frederik David Kan Bosch worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He headed the Archaeological Service of the Netherlands East Indies (~1916–1936) and held academic posts at Utrecht University (1938–1945) and Leiden University (1946–1957).

Fredrik Barth studied at the University of Chicago and under Edmund Leach at Cambridge. He held professorships at Bergen (1961–1972), Oslo (1974), and Boston University (~1997–2008), and also taught at Emory and Harvard (~1989–1996).
Friederike Assandri is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. She studied at the University of Heidelberg under Günther-Dietz Sontheimer and held a post there (attested 2013).

Friedhelm Hardy was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who completed doctoral work at the University of Oxford (1967). He served as Professor of Indian Religions at King's College London (~1975–2004) and as Wilde Lecturer at Oxford (1985–1987).

Friedrich Alexander Bischoff worked in Sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, earning doctorates at the University of Paris under Marcelle Lalou and Robert des Rotours. He held posts at Indiana University (1964–1982), University of Hamburg (1982–1993), and University of Vienna (~1983–2009).

Friedrich August Rosen was an Indologist and linguist who studied in Leipzig and Berlin under Franz Bopp. He was a professor of Oriental languages at UCL (1828–1831) and professor of Sanskrit at the University of London (1834).

Friedrich August Wolf was a linguist and historian who studied at the University of Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne (~1777–1779). He subsequently held a post at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1783–1807).

Friedrich Bechtel was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Theodor Benfey and August Fick at Heidelberg and Göttingen. After lecturing at Göttingen (1884), he served as professor of comparative linguistics at Halle from 1895.

Friedrich Benedict Weber studied at the University of Leipzig (~1792–1799). He held a post at European University Viadrina (~1802–1811) and served as professor of political economy at the University of Breslau (~1811–1848).

Friedrich Bollensen was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Heinrich Ewald at Göttingen. He served as adjunct professor at Saint Petersburg (~1842–1889) and as ordinary professor of Sanskrit at Kazan Federal University (1852–1856).

Friedrich Brockhaus was a professor who held academic posts at the University of Jena (~1868–1871), University of Basel (~1871–1872), Kiel University (~1872–1888), and the University of Marburg (~1888–1889).

Friedrich Carl Andreas worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (~1868–1870) and held posts at the University of Berlin (~1887–1903) and the University of Göttingen (~1903–1930).
